title: A conditional regulated generalized second law

items.title: Nested finite regulator and gravitational balance premises
items.physical_scope: An adopted finite-dimensional model on one fixed smooth classical Lorentzian background and an ordered pair of compact spacelike sections of one smooth null horizon. The outside density matrices, faithful reference matrices, geometric entropy values, factor nesting, and balance relation are specified model data. The reference-subtracted entropy is finite at each named regulator. No continuum factorization, physical state evolution, area calibration, regulator independence, or generalized second law for semiclassical gravity is asserted.
items.statement:
Fix a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $\mathcal H\subset M$ be a smooth embedded null hypersurface, meaning the induced metric on each $T_p\mathcal H$ has a one-dimensional radical. Supply a smooth nonzero future-directed null generator field $k$ in this radical with $\nabla_k k=0$. Choose nonempty compact smooth embedded spacelike two-surfaces $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2\subset\mathcal H$ transverse to $k$, so $T_p\Sigma_i\oplus\mathbb Rk_p=T_p\mathcal H$ for every $p\in\Sigma_i$. Their supplied family labels $t_1<t_2$ order the cuts; these geometric data use the horizon-section and affine-generator conventions of [[def-tgr-regulated-generalized-entropy]], but no global event-horizon property is assumed.

At a named finite regulator, take nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_2,H_E$ as the model outside Hilbert factors at $\Sigma_2$ and the additional region between the cuts, respectively, and use the ordered factorization $H_1=H_2\otimes H_E$ at $\Sigma_1$. Supply dimensionless density operators $\rho_1,\sigma_1$ on $H_1$ and $\rho_2,\sigma_2$ on $H_2$ such that $\rho_2=\operatorname{Tr}_E\rho_1$ and $\sigma_2=\operatorname{Tr}_E\sigma_1$. Require both $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ to be positive definite; the $\rho_i$ may have zero eigenvalues.

For each $i=1,2$, define $K_i:=-\log\sigma_i$ by finite-dimensional spectral calculus and $s(\tau):=-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)$ in nats, with $0\log0:=0$. Set $\Delta_i:=\operatorname{tr}((\rho_i-\sigma_i)K_i)$. Supply finite real geometric-entropy data $a_i$ in nats and adopt the balance premise

$$a_2-a_1=\Delta_1-\Delta_2.$$

With the physical Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in SI units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the model's reference-subtracted finite generalized entropy by

$$S_{\mathrm{gen},i}:=k_B\bigl[a_i+s(\rho_i)-s(\sigma_i)\bigr].$$

For a named sequence of regulators, impose these finite-dimensional premises term by term under one fixed subtraction and finite-normalization scheme. This adoption supplies no convergence claim. The scalar $a_i$ is model data; it is not thereby identified with an area term or with a calibrated gravitational entropy.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete article; §1, equations (1)–(3), §2.5, equations (38)–(43), and §2.8, equation (50). These sections motivate the finite balance and state the additional continuum and renormalization qualifications; they do not prove this adopted finite model premise.

references.locator: Complete 149-page PDF; §§10.8–10.9, printed pp. 146–147, equation (10.113), for the generalized-entropy summary and its stated backreaction limitation. The summary is context, not a proof of the adopted balance.

items.title: Regulated generalized entropy monotonicity under explicit balance
items.physical_scope: A conditional deduction for the finite-dimensional nested-regulator model with faithful reference states and the adopted modular-geometric balance. The finite-regulator inequality is pointwise in the named data. A limiting inequality is concluded only when both endpoint entropy sequences have finite limits in the same fixed scheme. The result does not assert limit existence, scheme independence, continuum quantum field theory, physical evolution, semiclassical backreaction, or an unrestricted generalized second law.
items.statement:
For every finite-regulator data set satisfying the nested balance postulate, set $D_i:=D(\rho_i\|\sigma_i)$ for $i=1,2$. Then

$$S_{\mathrm{gen},2}-S_{\mathrm{gen},1}=k_B\bigl[D(\rho_1\|\sigma_1)-D(\rho_2\|\sigma_2)\bigr]\ge0.$$

If a sequence of such data sets satisfies the postulate term by term under one fixed scheme, and both endpoint sequences converge to finite real values $S_{\mathrm{gen},i,n}\to L_i$, then $L_2\ge L_1$.

references.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6
references.locator: Complete article; §2.5, equations (38)–(43), and §2.8, equation (50). Wall's physical proof has separate horizon-algebra, semiclassical, and renormalization hypotheses and is not the proof of this finite conditional result.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)
references.locator: Complete 149-page PDF; §§10.8–10.9, printed pp. 146–147, equation (10.113), for the generalized-entropy summary and its backreaction qualification. This summary supplies context only.

title: A conditional regulated generalized second law — Examples

items.title: Finite product environment verifies conditional balance
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional product-state example inside the adopted nested horizon-balance model, including a two-dimensional worked instance. It makes no claim about a black-hole solution, continuum quantum field theory, empirical observation, or actual physical evolution.
items.statement: Let $H_2,H_E$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Let $\rho_2,\sigma_2$ be density operators on $H_2$ and $\rho_E,\sigma_E$ density operators on $H_E$, with $\sigma_2$ and $\sigma_E$ positive definite. Set $H_1:=H_2\otimes H_E$, $\rho_1:=\rho_2\otimes\rho_E$, and $\sigma_1:=\sigma_2\otimes\sigma_E$. Put $K_E:=-\log\sigma_E$ and $\Delta_E:=\operatorname{tr}((\rho_E-\sigma_E)K_E)$. Then $D(\rho_1\|\sigma_1)-D(\rho_2\|\sigma_2)=D(\rho_E\|\sigma_E)$, and the adopted geometric balance gives $S_{\mathrm{gen},2}-S_{\mathrm{gen},1}=k_BD(\rho_E\|\sigma_E)$. In the particular case $H_2=H_E=\mathbb C^2$ with $\langle z,w\rangle=z_0\overline{w_0}+z_1\overline{w_1}$, let $I_2$ be the identity map, take $\rho_2=\sigma_2=I_2/2$ and $\sigma_E=I_2/2$, and define $\rho_E:\mathbb C^2\to\mathbb C^2$ by $\rho_E(z_0,z_1):=(z_0,0)$. Then one has $\Delta_E=0$ and $D(\rho_E\|\sigma_E)=\log2$, so $a_2=a_1$ satisfies the balance premise and $S_{\mathrm{gen},2}-S_{\mathrm{gen},1}=k_B\log2$.
